newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes at weakest level of year.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes at weakest level of year.

text.p: The Mexican peso MXAAA closed at its weakest level this year on Friday, after another session punctuated by nerves and speculation, traders said.
The peso did recover slightly from session lows as dealers sold positions towards the close, traders added.
"The panic and (dollar) buying we saw this morning gave way a little at midsession, so some dealers sold positions they had bought," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 5.3 and 6.25 centavos weaker, at 7.9150/7.9250 and 7.90/7.92 per dollar, respectively.
The 48-hour peso had reached 7.9550/7.9750 per dollar at its weakest point during the session, its weakest level since November 1995. The spot peso ended the year at 7.7 per dollar.

The spot peso closed the week 19.1 centavos, or 2.41 percent, weaker than last Friday, when it closed at 7.7280/7.7340 per dollar. The same-day peso had earlier closed 11.65 centavos weaker at 7.9250/7.9300 per dollar.
Other traders suspected that the financial authorities may have bought dollars in late trade.
"We noticed that each time the peso looked like weakening to beyond 7.97 per dollar, dollars were suddenly on offer," said a trader.
Traders said jitters and speculation arose in early trading because of uncertainty over the forthcoming renewal of the "pacto".

The "pacto" is a series of economic measures agreed between government, business and labor leaders to control inflation and wage rises. The latest version of the "pacto" is known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery (ARE), was due to be renewed on Saturday, the president's office said.
"The problem is that the market is volatile in the run up to the ARE," the trader added, explaining in part the volatility.
